1.1.text:
Article 17

1. The Regional Government provides comprehensive protection to women from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Discrimination;
c. Violence; and
d. Exploitation.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a which is carried out either verbally or non-verbally that is intentionally directed at women so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
3. Every form of Discrimination act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b which is carried out leading to gender, racial, or equality injustice so as to degrade the status, freedom and opportunities of women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
4. Every form of Violence act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c which is carried out either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
5. Every form of Exploitation act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d which is carried out in any form that degrades the dignity, honor, and dignity of women and causes harm to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

Article 19

1. Social security as referred to in Article 18 letter a is carried out by the Regional Government together with the Village/Sub-district Government, Business Sector, and community.
2. Social security as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out by:
a. reporting if there is information on the occurrence of acts of threats of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against women;
b. implementing protection for Women Victims of acts of threats of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation;
c. providing Assistance and empowerment to Women Victims of acts of threats, Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation; and/or
d. securing perpetrators of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against Women who have the potential to endanger life safety.

Article 29

1. The Regional Government shall provide active and comprehensive protection to children from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Violence;
c. Exploitation;
d. neglect;
e. Child Maltreatment; and
f. Injustice.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a that is carried out either verbally or non-verbally that is intentionally directed at children so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
3. Every form of violent act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b that is carried out either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
4. Every form of exploitative act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c that is carried out in any form andnot in accordance with the child's developmental age according to general views, laws and regulations or local wisdom and causes harm to the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
5. Every form of neglectful act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d so as to neglect the responsibility as a parent, guardian, or foster parent toward the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
6. Every form of maltreatment act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e that is carried out by taking advantage of closeness or abuse of responsibility toward the child so as to cause physical or psychological trauma or is deemed contrary to laws and regulations is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
7. Every form of unjust act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter f, that is carried out by parents toward children who discriminate or show favoritism as well as injustice in equality between men and women.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Purworejo Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Purworejo. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Technical Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. 6. Village is a village and customary village or called by another name, hereinafter referred to as Village, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and administer governmental affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia and located in Purworejo Regency. 7. Village Government is the Village Head or called by another name who is assisted by village apparatus as an element of Village Government administration. 8. Sub-district is part of the territory of the District as a District apparatus. 9. Female Victim is a woman who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses resulting from gender-based violence, exploitation and/or discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life. 10. Child Victim is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses resulting from violence, exploitation and/or discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life. 11. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 13. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion either direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 14. Violence is any act of abuse of physical force with or without the use of means, unlawfully and causing misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 16. Child Maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted namely parents, close family, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions. 17. Prevention is all efforts to prevent Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation, as well as recurrence of occurrences against Women and Children. 18. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect which includes complaint Services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 19. Assistance is all efforts and actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect of Women and Children to resolve the problems faced so as to provide a sense of security and comfort and have readiness and/or ability to obtain Services and live their lives. 20. Assistant is a person or group or organization that is trusted and/or has the skills and knowledge to assist Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation with the aim that Female Victims and Child Victims feel safe and comfortable in accessing Services. 21. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Maltreatment, neglect and other problems. 22. Forum for the Protection of Violence Victims hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for Prevention, handling and empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Violence and other problems whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and established at the Regional, District, and Village levels. 23.

Article 32

1. The Regional Government together with the Village Government, community, and the Business World carry out social security.
2. Social security as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. reporting if there is information on Violence, Exploitation, neglect and/or Maltreatment of Children;
b. protection of child witnesses and Child Victims by keeping them away from perpetrators in temporary care facilities;
c. Assistance to Child Victims; and
d. securing perpetrators of violence who have the potential to endanger life safety.

Article 25

1. Physical and psychological health for Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation is intended to reduce and treat physical and psychological trauma.
2. FKPP shall facilitate or provide Assistance or handling of Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation.

Article 3

The implementation of protection for women and children is intended to provide a legal basis for implementing integrated and comprehensive protection for women and children and to realize synergy between the Regional Government and the community in protecting women and children as vulnerable groups who are susceptible to becoming victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Mistreatment and/or neglect towards a Women-Friendly and Child-Friendly Regency.

Article 26

1. Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect who experience trauma shall undergo a gradual rehabilitation process physically, psychologically, and socially.
2. Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
3. The Regional Government shall guarantee the fulfillment of living needs of Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect during the rehabilitation process.

Article 38

1. Child Victims of acts of Violence, Exploitation, Maltreatment of Children, and/or neglect who experience trauma undergo rehabilitation in stages both physically, psychologically, and socially.
2. Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
3. The Regional Government guarantees the living needs of Child Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) during the rehabilitation process.
4. During the rehabilitation process, the provision of food intake, education, play world, and appreciation for children who experience trauma as referred to in paragraph (1) is adjusted to age and developmental needs.

b. Violence;
c. Exploitation;

3. Every form of violent act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b that is carried out either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
4. Every form of exploitative act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c that is carried out in any form andnot in accordance with the child's developmental age according to general views, laws and regulations or local wisdom and causes harm to the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

6. Every form of maltreatment act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e that is carried out by taking advantage of closeness or abuse of responsibility toward the child so as to cause physical or psychological trauma or is deemed contrary to laws and regulations is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

1. Physical and psychological health for Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation is intended to reduce and treat physical and psychological trauma.
2. FKPP shall facilitate or provide Assistance or handling of Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation.

Article 26

1. Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect who experience trauma shall undergo a gradual rehabilitation process physically, psychologically, and socially.
2. Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
3. The Regional Government shall guarantee the fulfillment of living needs of Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect during the rehabilitation process.

Article 27

1. The provision of Restitution shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. The amount of Restitution paid by the perpetrator to Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect or their heirs shall be based on:a. the results of mediation agreement; and/orb. court decision.
3. The Regional Government through related Regional Apparatus shall oversee the Restitution payment process to ensure it is appropriate and on target.

Article 3

The implementation of protection for women and children is intended to provide a legal basis for implementing integrated and comprehensive protection for women and children and to realize synergy between the Regional Government and the community in protecting women and children as vulnerable groups who are susceptible to becoming victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Mistreatment and/or neglect towards a Women-Friendly and Child-Friendly Regency.

I. GENERAL

Constitutionally, the purpose of the state is none other than to protect the entire nation, advance general welfare, and educate the life of the nation. This is clearly stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The phrase protecting the entire nation contains a philosophical as well as moral dimension, where the state without discrimination must be able to be the protector of all its people. This commitment must be realized in various regulations and policies made by the state, so that it is no longer something that can be negotiated.

As is known, the position of women and children is very vulnerable to various kinds of violations including violations of their basic rights. Strategic steps need to be taken supported by policies, such as socializing the importance of protection and at the same time fulfilling their rights both in the family, community and at every level of education. The rights and protection of women and children are basically also mandated in the 1945 Constitution, so it has become the duty and responsibility of the state to protect them. The presence of the state in this context can be realized not only by the central government, but also by Regional Governments.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. The policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

Paragraph 3

Provision of Supporting Facilities and Infrastructure for the Protection of Women

Article 17

1. The Regional Government provides comprehensive protection to women from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Discrimination;
c. Violence; and
d. Exploitation.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a which is carried out either verbally or non-verbally that is intentionally directed at women so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
3. Every form of Discrimination act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b which is carried out leading to gender, racial, or equality injustice so as to degrade the status, freedom and opportunities of women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
4. Every form of Violence act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c which is carried out either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
5. Every form of Exploitation act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d which is carried out in any form that degrades the dignity, honor, and dignity of women and causes harm to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

Article 25

1. Physical and psychological health for Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation is intended to reduce and treat physical and psychological trauma.
2. FKPP shall facilitate or provide Assistance or handling of Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation.

Article 32

3. The Village/Sub-district Government may establish special institutions to organize the protection of women and children.

Article 17

1. The Regional Government provides comprehensive protection to women from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Discrimination;
c. Violence; and
d. Exploitation.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a which is carried out either verbally or non-verbally that is intentionally directed at women so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
3. Every form of Discrimination act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b which is carried out leading to gender, racial, or equality injustice so as to degrade the status, freedom and opportunities of women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
4. Every form of Violence act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c which is carried out either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
5. Every form of Exploitation act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d which is carried out in any form that degrades the dignity, honor, and dignity of women and causes harm to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

I. GENERAL

Constitutionally, the purpose of the state is none other than to protect the entire nation, advance general welfare, and educate the life of the nation. This is clearly stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The phrase protecting the entire nation contains a philosophical as well as moral dimension, where the state without discrimination must be able to be the protector of all its people. This commitment must be realized in various regulations and policies made by the state, so that it is no longer something that can be negotiated.

As is known, the position of women and children is very vulnerable to various kinds of violations including violations of their basic rights. Strategic steps need to be taken supported by policies, such as socializing the importance of protection and at the same time fulfilling their rights both in the family, community and at every level of education. The rights and protection of women and children are basically also mandated in the 1945 Constitution, so it has become the duty and responsibility of the state to protect them. The presence of the state in this context can be realized not only by the central government, but also by Regional Governments.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. The policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

Letter a

CHAPTER IV

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Part One General

Article 10

The Regional Government through Technical Regional Apparatus, the community, the Business World, parents and/or guardians have duties and responsibilities in providing protection for women and children so that welfare is realized both physically, spiritually, and socially.

I. GENERAL

Constitutionally, the purpose of the state is none other than to protect the entire nation, advance general welfare, and educate the life of the nation. This is clearly stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The phrase protecting the entire nation contains a philosophical as well as moral dimension, where the state without discrimination must be able to be the protector of all its people. This commitment must be realized in various regulations and policies made by the state, so that it is no longer something that can be negotiated.

As is known, the position of women and children is very vulnerable to various kinds of violations including violations of their basic rights. Strategic steps need to be taken supported by policies, such as socializing the importance of protection and at the same time fulfilling their rights both in the family, community and at every level of education. The rights and protection of women and children are basically also mandated in the 1945 Constitution, so it has become the duty and responsibility of the state to protect them. The presence of the state in this context can be realized not only by the central government, but also by Regional Governments.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. The policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. The policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

Article 29

1. The Regional Government shall provide active and comprehensive protection to children from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Violence;
c. Exploitation;
d. neglect;
e. Child Maltreatment; and
f. Injustice.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a that is carried out either verbally or non-verbally that is intentionally directed at children so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
3. Every form of violent act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b that is carried out either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
4. Every form of exploitative act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c that is carried out in any form andnot in accordance with the child's developmental age according to general views, laws and regulations or local wisdom and causes harm to the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
5. Every form of neglectful act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d so as to neglect the responsibility as a parent, guardian, or foster parent toward the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
6. Every form of maltreatment act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e that is carried out by taking advantage of closeness or abuse of responsibility toward the child so as to cause physical or psychological trauma or is deemed contrary to laws and regulations is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
7. Every form of unjust act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter f, that is carried out by parents toward children who discriminate or show favoritism as well as injustice in equality between men and women.

Article 17

1. The Regional Government provides comprehensive protection to women from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Discrimination;
c. Violence; and
d. Exploitation.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a which is carried out either verbally or non-verbally that is intentionally directed at women so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
3. Every form of Discrimination act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b which is carried out leading to gender, racial, or equality injustice so as to degrade the status, freedom and opportunities of women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
4. Every form of Violence act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c which is carried out either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
5. Every form of Exploitation act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d which is carried out in any form that degrades the dignity, honor, and dignity of women and causes harm to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

Article 19

1. Social security as referred to in Article 18 letter a is carried out by the Regional Government together with the Village/Sub-district Government, Business Sector, and community.
2. Social security as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out by:
a. reporting if there is information on the occurrence of acts of threats of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against women;
b. implementing protection for Women Victims of acts of threats of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation;
c. providing Assistance and empowerment to Women Victims of acts of threats, Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation; and/or
d. securing perpetrators of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against Women who have the potential to endanger life safety.

I. GENERAL

Constitutionally, the purpose of the state is none other than to protect the entire nation, advance general welfare, and educate the life of the nation. This is clearly stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The phrase protecting the entire nation contains a philosophical as well as moral dimension, where the state without discrimination must be able to be the protector of all its people. This commitment must be realized in various regulations and policies made by the state, so that it is no longer something that can be negotiated.

As is known, the position of women and children is very vulnerable to various kinds of violations including violations of their basic rights. Strategic steps need to be taken supported by policies, such as socializing the importance of protection and at the same time fulfilling their rights both in the family, community and at every level of education. The rights and protection of women and children are basically also mandated in the 1945 Constitution, so it has become the duty and responsibility of the state to protect them. The presence of the state in this context can be realized not only by the central government, but also by Regional Governments.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. The policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

Article 38

Article 29

1. The Regional Government shall provide active and comprehensive protection to children from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Violence;
c. Exploitation;
d. neglect;
e. Child Maltreatment; and
f. Injustice.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a that is carried out either verbally or non-verbally that is intentionally directed at children so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
3. Every form of violent act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b that is carried out either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

6. The implementation of protection for women and children is intended to provide a legal basis for implementing integrated and comprehensive protection for women and children and to realize synergy between the Regional Government and the community in protecting women and children as vulnerable groups who are susceptible to becoming victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Mistreatment and/or neglect towards a Women-Friendly and Child-Friendly Regency.

Part Four

Duties and Responsibilities of the Business World

I. GENERAL

Constitutionally, the purpose of the state is none other than to protect the entire nation, advance general welfare, and educate the life of the nation. This is clearly stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The phrase protecting the entire nation contains a philosophical as well as moral dimension, where the state without discrimination must be able to be the protector of all its people. This commitment must be realized in various regulations and policies made by the state, so that it is no longer something that can be negotiated.

As is known, the position of women and children is very vulnerable to various kinds of violations including violations of their basic rights. Strategic steps need to be taken supported by policies, such as socializing the importance of protection and at the same time fulfilling their rights both in the family, community and at every level of education. The rights and protection of women and children are basically also mandated in the 1945 Constitution, so it has become the duty and responsibility of the state to protect them. The presence of the state in this context can be realized not only by the central government, but also by Regional Governments.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. The policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

I. GENERAL

Constitutionally, the purpose of the state is none other than to protect the entire nation, advance general welfare, and educate the life of the nation. This is clearly stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The phrase protecting the entire nation contains a philosophical as well as moral dimension, where the state without discrimination must be able to be the protector of all its people. This commitment must be realized in various regulations and policies made by the state, so that it is no longer something that can be negotiated.

As is known, the position of women and children is very vulnerable to various kinds of violations including violations of their basic rights. Strategic steps need to be taken supported by policies, such as socializing the importance of protection and at the same time fulfilling their rights both in the family, community and at every level of education. The rights and protection of women and children are basically also mandated in the 1945 Constitution, so it has become the duty and responsibility of the state to protect them. The presence of the state in this context can be realized not only by the central government, but also by Regional Governments.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. The policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

I. GENERAL

Constitutionally, the purpose of the state is none other than to protect the entire nation, advance general welfare, and educate the life of the nation. This is clearly stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The phrase protecting the entire nation contains a philosophical as well as moral dimension, where the state without discrimination must be able to be the protector of all its people. This commitment must be realized in various regulations and policies made by the state, so that it is no longer something that can be negotiated.

As is known, the position of women and children is very vulnerable to various kinds of violations including violations of their basic rights. Strategic steps need to be taken supported by policies, such as socializing the importance of protection and at the same time fulfilling their rights both in the family, community and at every level of education. The rights and protection of women and children are basically also mandated in the 1945 Constitution, so it has become the duty and responsibility of the state to protect them. The presence of the state in this context can be realized not only by the central government, but also by Regional Governments.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. The policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

Paragraph 3

Provision of Facilities and Infrastructure

I. GENERAL

Constitutionally, the purpose of the state is none other than to protect the entire nation, advance general welfare, and educate the life of the nation. This is clearly stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The phrase protecting the entire nation contains a philosophical as well as moral dimension, where the state without discrimination must be able to be the protector of all its people. This commitment must be realized in various regulations and policies made by the state, so that it is no longer something that can be negotiated.

As is known, the position of women and children is very vulnerable to various kinds of violations including violations of their basic rights. Strategic steps need to be taken supported by policies, such as socializing the importance of protection and at the same time fulfilling their rights both in the family, community and at every level of education. The rights and protection of women and children are basically also mandated in the 1945 Constitution, so it has become the duty and responsibility of the state to protect them. The presence of the state in this context can be realized not only by the central government, but also by Regional Governments.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. The policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

Article 32

b. protection of child witnesses and Child Victims by keeping them away from perpetrators in temporary care facilities;
c. Assistance to Child Victims; and
d. securing perpetrators of violence who have the potential to endanger life safety.

1. Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect who experience trauma shall undergo a gradual rehabilitation process physically, psychologically, and socially.
2. Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
3. The Regional Government shall guarantee the fulfillment of living needs of Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect during the rehabilitation process.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Purworejo Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Purworejo. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Technical Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. 6. Village is a village and customary village or called by another name, hereinafter referred to as Village, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and administer governmental affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia and located in Purworejo Regency. 7. Village Government is the Village Head or called by another name who is assisted by village apparatus as an element of Village Government administration. 8. Sub-district is part of the territory of the District as a District apparatus. 9. Female Victim is a woman who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses resulting from gender-based violence, exploitation and/or discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life. 10. Child Victim is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses resulting from violence, exploitation and/or discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life. 11. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 13. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion either direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 14. Violence is any act of abuse of physical force with or without the use of means, unlawfully and causing misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 16. Child Maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted namely parents, close family, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions. 17. Prevention is all efforts to prevent Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation, as well as recurrence of occurrences against Women and Children. 18. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect which includes complaint Services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 19. Assistance is all efforts and actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect of Women and Children to resolve the problems faced so as to provide a sense of security and comfort and have readiness and/or ability to obtain Services and live their lives. 20. Assistant is a person or group or organization that is trusted and/or has the skills and knowledge to assist Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation with the aim that Female Victims and Child Victims feel safe and comfortable in accessing Services. 21. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Maltreatment, neglect and other problems. 22. Forum for the Protection of Violence Victims hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for Prevention, handling and empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Violence and other problems whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and established at the Regional, District, and Village levels. 23.

CHAPTER XVI

OTHER PROVISIONS

Article 55

1. In the event of changes to the nomenclature, duties, functions, and authority of Regional Apparatus, the accountability as regulated in this Regional Regulation shall automatically remain binding by adjusting proportionally to its duties and functions.
2. In the event of unclear division of duties, functions, and authority as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent shall appoint the Regional Apparatus most appropriate to carry out such obligation or responsibility.

Article 48

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the Business World, educational institutions or non-governmental institutions to organize the protection of women and children in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. socialization and counseling;
b. education and training;
c. legal aid; and/or
d. health and rehabilitation.

Article 32

1. The Regional Government together with the Village Government, community, and the Business World carry out social security.
2. Social security as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. reporting if there is information on Violence, Exploitation, neglect and/or Maltreatment of Children;
b. protection of child witnesses and Child Victims by keeping them away from perpetrators in temporary care facilities;
c. Assistance to Child Victims; and
d. securing perpetrators of violence who have the potential to endanger life safety.

Article 29

1. The Regional Government shall provide active and comprehensive protection to children from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Violence;
c. Exploitation;
d. neglect;
e. Child Maltreatment; and
f. Injustice.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a that is carried out either verbally or non-verbally that is intentionally directed at children so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
3. Every form of violent act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b that is carried out either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
4. Every form of exploitative act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c that is carried out in any form andnot in accordance with the child's developmental age according to general views, laws and regulations or local wisdom and causes harm to the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
5. Every form of neglectful act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d so as to neglect the responsibility as a parent, guardian, or foster parent toward the child is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
6. Every form of maltreatment act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e that is carried out by taking advantage of closeness or abuse of responsibility toward the child so as to cause physical or psychological trauma or is deemed contrary to laws and regulations is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
7. Every form of unjust act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter f, that is carried out by parents toward children who discriminate or show favoritism as well as injustice in equality between men and women.
